title: The flavor text tree: lines gated on stored conditions, walked so only options that work are gathered (GEN.1430)
rules: Gates read the stored quantities named in flavor_tree.QUANTITIES and the quantity table of oddities.json, never a class letter. A gate is a list of tests joined by 'and' (quantity with min, lt, equals or not_equals, the form of planet_class_fit.json and oddities.json); a node inherits the gates above it. Line ids are permanent: the first four families keep the keys they were stored under (habitable:N, planet:N, orbital:N, system:N), a removed line stays with 'retired' true so old rows still read. A node tagged ancient_works is skipped when the galaxy plan turns that family off.

lines.text: a derelict chain of deep-space platforms. They fire strong energy beams into the void for no known reason.
an automated buoy with a mass driver. It catches data pods and flings them toward the inner system.
a huge, thin sheet of reflective foil adrift in the system. It was once set up to shade a world.
thousands of small, passive reflectors scattered across the system. They bounce radio waves back and forth.
an ancient navigation beacon at the edge of the system. It runs on nuclear power and is kept up by a local artificial intelligence.
a drifting cloud of mirror tiles that no one steers. It looks like a broken solar collection swarm.
a network of navigation satellites across the system. They keep shifting their orbits, guided by a swarm intelligence with no single center.
an unseen mass in an empty orbit. Navigation sensors register it, and it bends the space around it.
a round dead zone in deep space. Every scan, signal, and burst of radiation that enters it drops to nothing.
a jagged, glowing crack in space-time. It keeps venting energy into the void around it.
a network of automated defense satellites spread across the system.
an array of laser transceivers. They hold a steady, high-speed optical link with one another.
a swarm of automated solar collectors skimming the star's corona. They feed steady power to huge, fully charged battery arrays.
a half-built ring of solar collectors around the star. The gaps suggest the work was abandoned.
a cluster of dormant, self-replicating probes holding formation. Their fabrication cycles stopped partway through.
a derelict generation ship on a slow, decaying orbit. Its hull is dark, and its drive is cold after generations adrift.
a mirror array angled to turn the star's light pressure into a gentle push. It has come loose and is drifting.
a pair of gravitational lensing relays aimed at a target far beyond the system. They are still listening.
a broken ring segment holding a stable orbit by itself. It seems to wait for the rest of the structure to return.
a scattering of paired relay buoys. They still send signals to partners that fell silent long ago.
an automated probe holding station at the edge of the system. Its greeting message loops with no one to hear it.
a magnetic siphon rig drawing material from the star's outer layers. It is still running long after its operators left.
a shell of solar-collecting satellites in a wide, half-finished orbit. Their construction drones are nowhere to be found.
a massive hollow metallic cylinder embedded in the crust.
the crashed hull of a derelict pre-warp ship.
the crashed hull of a derelict primitive warp ship.
a solar-powered beacon looping a brief audio distress call.
an array of automated radio dishes tracking empty coordinates in deep space.
a vast, precise grid of ancient cargo containers showing faint energy readings.
an abandoned solar farm attached to overfilled battery capacitors that periodically discharge themselves in violent plasma arcs.
a vast, perfectly smooth glass crater with refined materials fused into its center.
an automated surface rover actively sorting stones by size and composition into a grid.
the collapsed base of a space elevator, its severed cable coiled across the surrounding terrain for kilometers.
a sealed cryogenic vault built into the bedrock, its status lights still cycling after some uncounted span of time.
a field of dormant terraforming seeders, half-buried and inert, that should have blanketed the world in engineered soil long ago.
a buried genetic seed vault with a collapsed access shaft, its contents unknown.
a standing obelisk of unidentified alloy on an otherwise featureless plain, untouched by weathering.
an abandoned colony's foundation grid, its structural bones outlining streets and buildings that were never raised.
the fallen anchor of an orbital elevator, its counterweight long gone, embedded deep in the crust.
an automated excavation still cutting the same exhausted mineral seam decades after it ran dry.
a scorched landing zone cleared by a controlled burn that was, by every visible sign, never used.
a shallow crater ringed with fused glass, the unmistakable signature of an old kinetic impact test.
several dead delivery drones and cargo pods in stable orbits.
a dense debris ring consisting of shattered hull wreckage, dormant escape pods, and thousands of desiccated corpses in identical hazard suits.
a non-sentient drone swarm operating via networked intelligence that actively intercepts passing vessels it flags as requiring extensive repairs.
a primitive interstellar probe caught in orbit.
a derelict light cruiser venting plasma slowly into the surrounding void.
a derelict transport ship whose severed bow trails forty kilometers behind its own stern.
a dense ring of cobalt-ferrite dust, in a thick fog of ionized sodium-potassium gas broadcasting radio signals across a variety of frequencies.
a monolithic stone sculpture of a humanoid hand orbiting with its index finger pointing at magnetic north.
a constellation of large solar mirrors suspended in a rough orbital grid.
a ring of cryostasis pods tumbling freely, their occupants' status unreadable at this range.
the wreckage of a one-sided battle, hulls scattered with no intact vessel among them.
a stationary listening post bristling with dish arrays, all aimed at a patch of empty sky.
a dormant ring-shaped gate of unfamiliar design, its inner surface dark and its function unconfirmed.
a cluster of sealed seed pods tumbling in a slow, decaying orbit, clearly not of local origin.
an automated checkpoint platform still broadcasting docking instructions in a language no database recognizes.
a field of armed kinetic interceptors, live and waiting, with no record of who deployed them.
a solitary dark-hulled relay emitting a tight beam toward the star and nothing else.
the fused, burned-out frame of an old drive test rig, its containment ring melted solid.
a loose formation of repair drones still patrolling a ship that no longer exists.
slimy films on wet rock at the water's edge, thickest where the light is strongest.
pale stains on the sea floor where mats have died and settled in thin layers.
green-gray mats that spread across the shallows and bubble oxygen into the water.
clouds of drifting single cells that tint the surface water in broad bands.
purple and green mats that stain the shallows, with a faint smell of methane in the air.
thick, layered mats in the shallows, rippling where gas rises through them.
microscopic airborne organisms that cause nighttime clouds to glow with blue bioluminescence.
tall, iron-rich trees that act as natural lightning rods to pop open their heat-activated seed pods.
lowland basins heavily blanketed in a thick yellow fog caused by massive fungal spore releases.
dense subterranean vines that register rapid, targeted growth vectors toward concentrated heat sources.
radiotrophic fungi that thrive in irradiated caverns, growing darker and denser near hot mineral veins.
dense colonies that cover rock in the shallows in layered crusts, banded green and brown.
tangled growth that forms floating rafts across calm water.
domes of living mat that float on trapped methane.
stands of tall, green growth in the shallows, swaying with the current.
armored, tortoise-like animals that eat raw rock and excrete exceptionally fine glass sand.
high-altitude predators with hyper-thin membranous wings that ride the solar wind.
jagged, forest-like continental structures built from the hard mineral shells of colonial insects.
massive, lighter-than-air floating beasts that use natural gas bladders to filter-feed on atmospheric plankton.
migratory animals that navigate along the electromagnetic hum of buried, abandoned colonial power grids.
pack hunters communicating via low-frequency infrasound that induces unexplained dread and vertigo in explorers.
large, eyeless amphibious predators observed actively tracking the dissolved chemical residue of engine exhaust.
colonial filter-feeders anchored to reef structures, pulsing in loose synchrony with the tides.
burrowing, desiccation-proof invertebrates that survive years dormant between rare rainfalls.
grazing animals with slowly crystallizing shells that eventually fuse into the rock formations they feed on.
blind cave-dwellers that navigate total darkness by sensing faint bioelectric fields in the walls around them.
lichen-like organisms that ride migrating herds, trading camouflage for transport.
herd animals that bury themselves and estivate for years to survive multi-year droughts.
predators whose skin patterns mimic local flora so precisely they vanish at rest.
colonial organisms that briefly link into a single distributed nervous system during seasonal migration.
subterranean dwellers that cultivate bacterial mats in lightless tunnels as a stable food source across generations.
pale communities in the dark that make methane from hydrogen and carbon dioxide, with no light at all.
deep wells in the rock that bubble with gas made by living communities.
mats that coat the rock around a vent, living on the chemical difference between the vent water and the sea.
slick films on rock in the dark, thickest where warm water seeps out.
white threads of living cells trailing in the water downstream of a seep.
dense colonies of chemical feeders around a vent field, banded white, orange, and black.
thick, pale mats that wrap the rock for kilometers along a seep.
pillars of mineral and living crust that rise from the sea floor above a vent.
beds of pale, ropy growth packed into cracks in the rock where warm water rises.
tube-like animals crowded around a vent, with clams and grazers among them.
small, pale grazers that swarm over the mats around a vent and scatter when the water changes.
clams and snails packed along a seep, each one fed by cells living inside it.
swarms of tiny, blind animals that drift up from the vents in the warm plume.
droplets in the cloud deck that carry living cells.
mats that line pools of concentrated acid and shed solid sulfur crusts.
silica-rimmed pools of acid where living mats slowly build white terraces.
yellow films on the rock above the acid, thickest where the vapor condenses.
dense colonies of living droplets in the cloud deck, thick enough to darken the layer.
thick mats on the acid pools, layered yellow and white.
crusts of sulfur and silica built up by mats around the rims of acid pools.
stringy growths that hang in the acid pools like curtains.
slow communities living in pools of liquid carbon dioxide, growing only a few millimeters in a year.
slow mats that take hydrogen as fuel and shed the water they make.
thin films on the rock around carbon dioxide seeps, thicker where hydrogen rises.
mats thick enough to see from a ridge, layered in dull gray and brown, on the floor of a carbon dioxide pool.
slow colonies that coat the rock around hydrogen seeps.
gray crusts at the edge of a carbon dioxide pool, growing a few centimeters in a century.
slow mats on the floor of a hydrocarbon sea, giving off methane as they feed on acetylene and hydrogen.
dark, slow communities in a sea of liquid methane, far too cold for water.
dark films in the shore pools, thickest where acetylene rains out of the air.
mats thick enough to see at the shore of a methane sea, dark brown and slow to change.
dark crusts that line the beds of hydrocarbon lakes.
tangled dark growth in the shallows of a methane lake, matted by the waves.
communities in veins of cold brine inside the ice.
slow colonies in brine channels under a thick ice lid.
dark threads of living cells frozen into the ice where brine pockets once lay.
thin films on the underside of the ice, where the brine meets the cold.
ropy mats in the brine channels, thick enough to slow the flow.
dark, branching colonies that fill the cracks in the ice.
layered mats on the underside of the ice, banded where the brine has risen and frozen again.
lit cities on the nightside, in bright webs along the coasts.
dense radio chatter across a wide band of the spectrum.
orbital traffic: a steady stream of ships leaving the surface and crossing between orbits.
a dark, cold world with no sun, drifting alone between the stars.
a sky with no daylight, only the faint glow of distant stars.
no sunrise and no sunset: the sky never changes.
banded clouds with no sunlight on them, glowing faintly in the infrared from the heat inside.
a gas giant with no star, its cloud bands lit by nothing but its own heat.
bare, frozen ground under a black sky, warmed only by heat from the rock below.
a deep ocean sealed under ice, kept liquid by heat from the rock below.
a moon in orbit that travels with it through the dark.
a small world in orbit around a larger one.
a host that hangs in one spot in the sky, never rising and never setting.
a host that rises and sets as the moon turns.
a wide ring of rock and ice debris that never gathered into a planet.
countless small bodies, so far apart that a ship could cross the ring without passing close to one.
a faint band of dust and rock chips, brightest where the pieces collide.
a field kept stirred by a giant's pull, with fresh collision debris across its width.
streams of broken rock thrown out of the ring by a giant's gravity.
one large, round body among the rubble, the biggest by far.
a belt heavy enough that its own pull shows in the motion of the planets near it.
a narrow ring with sharp edges, held in a thin line by the pull of a planet.
a point of light that holds steady, with only faint changes in brightness over the years.
a star that the sensors can place precisely, with nothing unusual in its light.
a star whose brightness wobbles slightly as spots cross its face.
a dim, red star that flares without warning and washes its inner worlds in ultraviolet light.
a faint red star with dark spots that cover much of its face.
a hot, blue star whose light drives a strong wind off its surface.
a bright blue star that burns through its fuel in a few million years.
a swollen star whose loose outer layers glow a deep red and drift away into space.
a young star still ringed by leftover gas and dust.
an old star, long past its restless youth and slowly changing.
a small, dark nucleus of ice and dust, darker than coal where the sunlight has baked its surface.
a loose body of frozen gas and dust that holds together only by its own faint pull.
a rough, pitted nucleus that sheds a little dust whenever its star warms it.
a bright coma and a long tail of dust and gas, pushed away from the star by its light.
jets of gas that leave the nucleus in narrow streams as the ice warms.
a nucleus only a few kilometers across, easy to break apart.
a path so close to the star that the surface is stripped away at every pass.
an orbit so stretched that the comet is only just bound to its star.
a point of nothing, circled by a thin ring of bent starlight.
a region where light cannot leave, marked only by its pull on nearby stars.
a silent, dark object that shows itself only by what it does to the light behind it.
a glowing disk of hot gas spiraling in, brighter on the side that moves toward you.
a hole spinning near its limit, dragging space around with it.
a giant hole, heavy enough to hold a whole cluster of stars around it.
a ball of neutrons the size of a city, spinning in the dark.
a body smaller than a city and heavier than a star.
a crust so smooth that its tallest ridge is no higher than a grain of sand.
a beam of radio waves that sweeps past every few milliseconds, as steady as a clock.
a magnetic field so strong that it stretches the atoms near the surface into thin needles.
a surface hot enough to glow in X-rays.
a vast cloud of thin gas and dust, glowing where nearby stars light it.
dark lanes of dust that block the stars behind them.
slow currents of gas, stirred by the stars forming inside.
gas heated until it glows in sharp colors, red from hydrogen and green from oxygen.
cores so dense that new stars are forming in them.
a young cloud, still shaped by the stars that formed in it.
a cloud so wide that light needs decades to cross it.
a shell of hot gas, still racing outward from a star that exploded long ago.
thin filaments of glowing gas, torn from the star as it blew apart.
an expanding bubble that clears out the gas around it.
a young remnant, still bright in X-rays and still crashing through the gas around it.
a fading remnant, so large and old that it is blending into the gas around it.
a core that outshines its whole galaxy, fed by gas falling into a giant black hole.
a point of light brighter than billions of stars together.
a bright core wrapped in a thick doughnut of dust that hides the hole from the side.
twin jets of fast particles, running far out into space on both sides.
a jet longer than the galaxy that made it.
a core shining as brightly as its mass allows, its own light holding back the falling gas.
a small body of ice and rock adrift between the stars, cold and dark.
a nucleus that has not been near a sun in a very long time.
a quiet nucleus with no tail to show where it has been.
a faint tail, made by what little ice the distant starlight can warm.
a body moving much faster than the stars around it.
a loose swarm of rock fragments, spread across a volume wider than a star system.
pieces of rock that never fell into any star or planet.
a thin, drifting cloud of rock and dust.
fragments moving fast enough that a collision would shatter them.
one large body among the fragments, held together by its own pull.
